summary: German summary document of a summary plus appendix pair (T04 is the appendix), opened by a cover block with logo, contact box and patient block. It lists one-line questionnaire and test summaries, a few task and EEG figures, CP summary and discussion slots, an 81-row overview table that groups all results under condition labels, and empty diagnosis and recommendation areas with a signature placeholder. CP output is rare in practice (a handful of reports a year).

review_response.finding: pseudonymisation 0, 1, classify-4 0, numbers 1: quoted template prose slipped through a 5-word check that ignored hyphens and text boxes
review_response.reason: Ran a 4-word check (hyphens split) against all XML text of the raw docx, content controls, text boxes, footnotes and document properties included; no run of template prose remains in T05.

review_response.finding: pseudonymisation 2: close paraphrases of company-standard sentences (spike reading, group match, recommendation lead-in, medication line)
review_response.reason: Every fixed sentence is described by its function only (for example a fixed sentence stating a match with a diagnosed group whatever the computed result).

review_response.finding: pseudonymisation 5: exact brand colour values recorded
review_response.reason: Theme colours are plain colour names; no colour values.

review_response.finding: pseudonymisation 6: exact use counts allow re-identification
review_response.reason: reports_per_year and share_pct come from usage_rounded.json.

review_response.finding: classify-3 9: author names inside marker names and descriptions
review_response.reason: Markers that carry a person or questionnaire-author name are written with <author>; clinic codes inside markers as <clinic>, the company name as <company>, a place code as <place>.

review_response.finding: classify-2 3, completeness 0: extractor skipped content controls, so covers, running headers and preambles were missing
review_response.reason: Model rebuilt from tpl_extract_v2 (content controls and text boxes included) and checked against the raw XML of body, headers, footers, footnotes and relationships.

review_response.finding: classify-2 5, numbers 0, completeness 1: coverage counted only elements classed not_expressible while listed gaps sat in covered elements
review_response.reason: Every element whose representation needs a schema change is now class not_expressible with a gap code, one not_expressible entry per such element; counts equal the element classes.

review_response.finding: numbers 2, completeness 1: table of contents, language and control lines and manual ERP tables classed differently per modeller
review_response.reason: One rule: table of contents and page references not_expressible G5; language selectors, hidden lines and block markers leave_out control_marker; hand-ticked ERP tables not_expressible G6 (where present).

review_response.finding: classify-3 1, classify-4 5, numbers 4: fixed verdict sentences classed clinician or folded into other elements
review_response.reason: Each fixed verdict sentence is its own leave_out fixed_verdict element with claim wording set; none is a clinician starter.

review_response.finding: completeness 8: suggestions proposing clinic-written draft starters or verdict rows
review_response.reason: No suggestion in this model supports prefilled verdicts, treatment advice or condition rows; prefilled content is leave_out.

review_response.finding: classify-3 0, classify-1 3, 4, 5, 15, classify-4 4: legends and captions with mental-function labels folded into device elements as neutral
review_response.reason: Legends and captions next to core figures are split from the figure; neutral ones are clinic text (b1), those with mental-function labels or interpretation are clinic text with claim_wording true.

review_response.finding: classify-4 16, classify-3 5: static explanations inside non-core sections split in some models and folded in others
review_response.reason: One rule in this model: static text inside an open, later_module, research_only or dropped section takes that section's class with claim_wording set when it applies; fixed verdict sentences are split out everywhere.

review_response.finding: classify-1 6, classify-3 6: generated figure sentences of the task counted as device
